topics.name: Tawheed
topics.description: The indivisible oneness of Allah as the singular God, foundational to Islamic creed.

topics.name: Shirk
topics.description: The association of partners with Allah; the gravest violation of Tawheed in Islamic theology.

topics.name: Lordship of Allah
topics.description: Allah's exclusive sovereignty as creator, sustainer, and master of all existence (Rububiyyah).

topics.name: Names and Attributes of Allah
topics.description: The ninety-nine or more divine names and qualitative attributes that describe Allah's essence and actions.

topics.name: Worship of Allah Alone
topics.description: The exclusive direction of all acts of worship to Allah (Uluhiyyah), rejecting devotion to any other entity.

topics.name: Divine Majesty
topics.description: The transcendent greatness, glory, and awe-inspiring grandeur of Allah.

topics.name: Divine Perfection
topics.description: Allah's absolute flawlessness and transcendence above all deficiency or likeness to creation.

topics.name: Taghut
topics.description: False deities and powers worshipped or obeyed in defiance of Allah, rejecting Taghut is stated as the prerequisite condition alongside belief in Allah.

primary: rejecting false gods before believing in Allah
whoever rejects false deities and believes in Allah
idols and false powers worshipped besides Allah
secondary: those who seek judgment from false authorities
Satan leading people to false deities

topics.name: Alliance and Enmity in Faith
topics.description: The creedal dimension of allegiance, taking believers as allies and disavowing disbelief and its people, explicitly stated in multiple Quranic verses.

primary: prohibiting taking disbelievers as close allies
secondary: do not take disbelievers as awliya
bonds of faith over bonds of blood

topics.name: Divine Mercy
topics.description: Allah's encompassing compassion and forgiveness toward His creation, expressed through grace and pardon.

topics.name: Divine Knowledge
topics.description: Allah's omniscience, His complete and eternal awareness of all manifest and hidden things.

topics.name: Divine Power
topics.description: Allah's unlimited omnipotence and absolute ability over all things.

topics.name: Divine Wisdom
topics.description: Allah's perfect wisdom underlying all creation, command, and decree.

topics.name: Divine Justice
topics.description: Allah's perfect attribute of justice, His absolute fairness in judgment, decree, and recompense without any possibility of ظلم (injustice).

topics.name: Divine Will
topics.description: Allah's sovereign and unrestricted will over all that exists and all that occurs.

topics.name: Divine Signs
topics.description: Observable phenomena in creation and scripture that serve as evidence of Allah's existence and attributes.

topics.name: Divine Hearing and Seeing
topics.description: Allah's absolute and complete perception of all sounds and sights without limitation.

topics.name: Angels
topics.description: Belief in the angelic beings created from light who execute Allah's commands and serve specific cosmic roles.

secondary: servants of Allah in the unseen

topics.name: Jinn
topics.description: Belief in the race of sentient beings created from smokeless fire, coexisting with but invisible to humans.

topics.name: Divine Books
topics.description: Belief in the scriptures revealed by Allah to His prophets as guidance for humanity.

topics.name: Belief in the Unseen
topics.description: The overarching creedal commitment to accepting realities not accessible through direct observation or empirical means.

topics.name: Preserved Tablet
topics.description: The divine record (Lawh al-Mahfuz) in which all of creation's events are eternally inscribed.

topics.name: Throne of Allah
topics.description: The Arsh and Kursi, the supreme metaphysical stations representing Allah's dominion over creation.

topics.name: Angels Recording Deeds
topics.description: The honourable scribing angels (Kiraman Katibin) assigned to record every human action.

topics.name: Divine Decree
topics.description: Allah's pre-eternal knowledge and ordainment of all events before creation.

topics.name: Human Free Will
topics.description: The capacity of humans to make real moral choices within the framework of divine decree.

topics.name: Trust in Allah
topics.description: Complete reliance upon and delegation of affairs to Allah (Tawakkul) after taking available means.

topics.name: Divine Testing
topics.description: Allah's purposeful subjection of believers to hardship or ease as a trial of faith and character.

topics.name: Contentment with Decree
topics.description: The spiritual state of being inwardly satisfied with whatever Allah has decreed.

topics.name: Faith
topics.description: Iman, the sincere inner conviction in the six articles of faith, expressed in word and deed.

topics.name: Disbelief
topics.description: Kufr, the rejection or denial of the fundamental truths of Islam.

topics.name: Hypocrisy
topics.description: Nifaq, outward profession of Islam concealing inner disbelief or treachery.

topics.name: Apostasy
topics.description: Riddah, the act of consciously abandoning or renouncing Islam after having accepted it.

topics.name: Certainty of Faith
topics.description: Yaqeen, the highest degree of unwavering conviction, free from doubt.

topics.name: Increase and Decrease of Faith
topics.description: The Sunni doctrine that Iman fluctuates in strength through obedience, reflection, and sin.

topics.name: Covenant with Allah
topics.description: The primordial pledge (Mithaq) taken from all human souls before creation, affirming Allah's lordship.

topics.name: Shahada
topics.description: The Islamic declaration of faith, the testimony that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger.

topics.name: Fitrah
topics.description: The innate primordial disposition of the human soul toward recognizing and inclining to Allah.

topics.name: Obligatory Prayer
topics.description: The five daily fard prayers (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha) obligatory upon every Muslim.

topics.name: Voluntary Prayer
topics.description: Supererogatory prayers (Nafl/Sunnah) performed beyond the obligatory, including the night prayer.

topics.name: Friday Prayer
topics.description: The obligatory congregational Jumu'ah prayer performed on Fridays, replacing Dhuhr.

topics.name: Prostration
topics.description: The act of Sujud, placing the forehead on the ground as the pinnacle of submission to Allah.

topics.name: Khushu in Prayer
topics.description: The state of deep humility, focus, and spiritual presence required in prayer.

topics.name: Direction of Prayer
topics.description: The Qiblah, the obligation to face the direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah during prayer.

topics.name: Prayer Times
topics.description: The five prescribed daily time intervals within which each obligatory prayer must be performed.

topics.name: Congregational Prayer
topics.description: Praying in a group (Jama'ah) behind an Imam, which carries increased spiritual reward.

topics.name: Adhaan, Call to Prayer
topics.description: The call to prayer referenced in the Quran, including the verse on those who mock the call and the command to hasten to prayer on Friday.

primary: hasten to the remembrance of Allah on Friday
those who mock the call to prayer
secondary: come to prayer come to success
leave trade and hasten to prayer

topics.name: Eid and Celebration
topics.description: The Quranic reference to a day of celebration, the disciples of Isa requesting a table spread as an Eid, and completing worship as a cause for communal glorification of Allah.

primary: disciples asking for a feast day
completing the fast and glorifying Allah
completing the count of days and thanking Allah

topics.name: Fasting in Ramadan
topics.description: The obligatory fast throughout the month of Ramadan, one of the five pillars of Islam.

topics.name: Voluntary Fasting
topics.description: Optional fasts performed on recommended days such as Mondays, Thursdays, or the fast of Dawud.

topics.name: Laylat al-Qadr
topics.description: The Night of Decree in the last ten nights of Ramadan, surpassing a thousand months in virtue.

topics.name: I'tikaf
topics.description: Spiritual seclusion in the mosque, especially in the last ten days of Ramadan.

topics.name: Self-Restraint through Fasting
topics.description: Fasting as a means of cultivating Taqwa through disciplined suppression of desires.

topics.name: Breaking the Fast
topics.description: The act of Iftar, ending the fast at sunset, and Suhur, the pre-dawn meal.

topics.name: Obligatory Charity
topics.description: Zakat, the annual compulsory alms on qualifying wealth, one of the five pillars of Islam.

topics.name: Voluntary Charity
topics.description: Sadaqah, any voluntary act of giving for Allah's sake, including non-monetary forms.

topics.name: Spending in the Way of Allah
topics.description: Infaq fi sabilillah, expending wealth in causes pleasing to Allah, including jihad, dawah, and welfare.

topics.name: Recipients of Charity
topics.description: The eight categories of eligible recipients of Zakat as defined in Quranic scripture.

topics.name: Pilgrimage to Makkah
topics.description: Hajj, the obligatory annual pilgrimage to Makkah and its sacred sites, fifth pillar of Islam.

topics.name: Umrah
topics.description: The lesser pilgrimage to Makkah performable at any time of year, not obligatory but highly recommended.

topics.name: Sacrifice
topics.description: Qurbani/Udhiyah, the ritual slaughter of livestock on Eid al-Adha commemorating Ibrahim's sacrifice.

topics.name: Tawaf
topics.description: The ritual circumambulation of the Ka'bah seven times, performed in Hajj and Umrah.

topics.name: Sa'i
topics.description: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwa seven times, commemorating Hajar's search for water.

topics.name: Remembrance of Allah
topics.description: Dhikr, the continuous verbal and mental glorification of Allah through prescribed and spontaneous phrases.

topics.name: Supplication
topics.description: Du'a, direct personal invocation and petition to Allah, described as the essence of worship.

topics.name: Seeking Forgiveness
topics.description: Istighfar, actively seeking Allah's forgiveness through repentance and verbal appeal.

topics.name: Gratitude to Allah
topics.description: Shukr, recognizing Allah as the source of blessings and expressing thankfulness through words, worship, and obedience.

topics.name: Praising Allah
topics.description: Hamd and Tasbih, specific acts of glorifying and extolling Allah's perfection.

topics.name: Sending Blessings on the Prophet
topics.description: Salawat, invoking Allah's blessings and peace upon the Prophet Muhammad.

topics.name: Ritual Purification
topics.description: Taharah, the ritual cleanliness achieved through Wudu, Ghusl, or Tayammum required for acts of worship.

topics.name: Cleanliness
topics.description: Nazafah, general bodily and environmental hygiene promoted as part of Islamic practice.

topics.name: Oaths
topics.description: Yameen, solemn swearing by Allah's name, with binding legal and moral implications.

secondary: not to swear by other than Allah

topics.name: Vows
topics.description: Nadhr, a voluntary pledge to Allah to perform an act conditional on a desire or as pure devotion.

topics.name: Expiation
topics.description: Kaffarah, prescribed acts of atonement for breaking oaths or other specific violations.

topics.name: Patience
topics.description: Sabr, steadfast endurance in the face of hardship, sin-avoidance, or the demands of obedience. A comprehensive moral virtue, not limited to any single context.

topics.name: Truthfulness
topics.description: Sidq, consistency between inner conviction and outward expression; honesty in all speech and conduct.

topics.name: Humility
topics.description: Tawadu, lowering oneself before Allah and avoiding arrogance toward other humans.

topics.name: Generosity
topics.description: Karam, freely giving wealth, time, and goodness beyond what is obligated.

topics.name: Courage
topics.description: Shuja'ah, the virtue of bravery in standing for truth and facing fear in Allah's cause.

topics.name: Gentleness
topics.description: Rifq, soft, kind, and considerate treatment of others as a prophetic character trait.

topics.name: Trustworthiness
topics.description: Amanah, reliability and faithfulness in honoring all trusts, covenants, and responsibilities.

topics.name: Righteousness
topics.description: Birr, comprehensive moral goodness encompassing piety, right action, and excellent conduct.

topics.name: Hayaa (Modesty and Shame)
topics.description: The virtue of modesty and protective shame, present in Quranic verses on lowering the gaze and in the depiction of the modest woman who approached Musa in Madyan.

primary: she came to him walking with shyness
modest woman in the story of Moses
secondary: lowering gaze as expression of modesty

topics.name: Chastity (Iffah)
topics.description: Restraining oneself from forbidden desires, praised in Joseph's resistance to seduction and in direct commands to guard one's chastity.

primary: I seek refuge in Allah from this
secondary: those who cannot marry should remain chaste

topics.name: Arrogance
topics.description: Kibr, an inflated sense of self-importance that blinds one to truth and breeds contempt for others.

topics.name: Envy
topics.description: Hasad, wishing the removal of another's blessing out of resentment or spite.

topics.name: Greed
topics.description: Tama and Shuh, excessive desire for wealth and possessions, paired with miserliness.

topics.name: Lying
topics.description: Kadhib, deliberate false speech, condemned as a root of all vices in Islamic ethics.

topics.name: Backbiting
topics.description: Gheebah, mentioning a person's real faults in their absence without need or justification.

topics.name: Injustice
topics.description: Dhulm, wrongdoing that transgresses the rights of Allah, the self, or other creation.

topics.name: Extravagance
topics.description: Israf and Tabdheer, wasteful excess in consumption or spending beyond need.

topics.name: Haste
topics.description: Ajalah, acting impulsively without deliberation, contrasted with the Islamic value of measured action.

topics.name: Forgiveness
topics.description: Afw, the act of pardoning others' offenses without requiring recompense.

topics.name: Good Companionship
topics.description: Selecting righteous and virtuous companions whose influence strengthens one's faith and character.

topics.name: Fulfilling Promises
topics.description: Wafa, the obligation to honor agreements and commitments made to others.

topics.name: Good Speech
topics.description: Qawl Hasanah, the Islamic standard of speaking words that are true, kind, and beneficial.

topics.name: Respecting Others
topics.description: Ikram, honoring human dignity and showing due respect to others regardless of status.

topics.name: Avoiding Suspicion
topics.description: Husn al-Dhann, cultivating good assumptions about others and avoiding baseless suspicion.

topics.name: Sincerity
topics.description: Ikhlas, performing deeds exclusively for Allah's sake, free from any desire for human recognition.

topics.name: Showing Off
topics.description: Riya, performing acts of worship to be seen or praised by people, nullifying their spiritual value.

topics.name: Correct Intention
topics.description: Niyyah, the deliberate, conscious purpose underlying an act that determines its religious validity.

topics.name: Self-Accountability
topics.description: Muhasabah, the practice of regularly examining one's own deeds, motives, and spiritual state.

topics.name: Love of Allah
topics.description: Hubb Allah, supreme devotional love for Allah that motivates obedience and transforms character.

topics.name: Compassion for Creation
topics.description: Rahmah, extending mercy, empathy, and care toward all of Allah's creatures.

topics.name: Brotherhood and Sisterhood
topics.description: Ukhuwwah, the bond of faith that unites believers as a single spiritual family.

topics.name: Kindness to Parents
topics.description: Birr al-Walidayn, dutiful, respectful, and loving treatment of one's parents as a supreme obligation.

topics.name: Marriage
topics.description: Nikah, the sacred contract of matrimony in Islam, establishing rights and obligations between spouses.

topics.name: Divorce
topics.description: Talaq and Khul, the lawful dissolution of marriage, governed by prescribed procedures and conditions.

topics.name: Rights of Spouses
topics.description: The mutual and reciprocal rights and obligations incumbent on husband and wife in Islamic law.

topics.name: Parenting
topics.description: Tarbiyah, the Islamic responsibility of raising children with proper moral, religious, and educational upbringing.

topics.name: Kinship Ties
topics.description: Silat al-Rahm, maintaining and nurturing bonds with extended family as a religious obligation.

topics.name: Orphan Care
topics.description: The Islamic duty to protect, care for, and justly manage the affairs of orphaned children.

topics.name: Fair Trade
topics.description: The Islamic ethic of honest, just, and transparent commercial dealings between parties.

topics.name: Prohibition of Riba
topics.description: The absolute Islamic prohibition of usury and interest-based transactions as exploitative and unjust.

topics.name: Wealth Management
topics.description: Islamic principles of responsible stewardship over financial resources and assets.

topics.name: Debt and Contracts
topics.description: Islamic rules governing the documentation, fulfilment, and ethics of loans and contractual agreements.

topics.name: Fraud and Cheating
topics.description: The Islamic prohibition of deceptive or manipulative practices in commercial and social dealings.

topics.name: Justice
topics.description: Adl, the comprehensive Islamic obligation to deal equitably and without bias in all affairs.

topics.name: Rights of the Poor
topics.description: The Islamic obligation to protect the welfare of the destitute and ensure their basic needs are met.

topics.name: Rights of Neighbors
topics.description: Haqq al-Jar, specific duties and courtesies owed to those who live in proximity.

topics.name: Equality
topics.description: Musawah, the Islamic principle that all humans are equal regardless of race, tribe, or lineage.

topics.name: Combating Oppression
topics.description: The Islamic duty to oppose, resist, and seek redress against all forms of tyranny and injustice.

topics.name: Consultation
topics.description: Shura, the Islamic principle of collective deliberation and seeking counsel in decision-making.

topics.name: Enjoining Good
topics.description: Amr bil Ma'ruf, the positive obligation to actively promote and encourage virtuous acts in society.

topics.name: Forbidding Evil
topics.description: Nahi anil Munkar, the obligation to oppose and prevent wrongdoing in society by appropriate means.

topics.name: Cooperation
topics.description: Ta'awun, mutual assistance and collaborative effort in righteousness among believers.

topics.name: Unity of the Ummah
topics.description: The imperative for Muslims to maintain communal solidarity and avoid division.

topics.name: Peace and Reconciliation
topics.description: Sulh and Islah, the Islamic imperative to resolve conflicts and restore harmony between parties.

topics.name: Inheritance Law
topics.description: Faraid, the divinely prescribed system of shares for distributing a deceased's estate.

topics.name: Bequests
topics.description: Wasiyyah, a testamentary gift of up to one-third of one's estate, directed to non-heirs before death.

topics.name: Wealth Circulation
topics.description: The Islamic principle that wealth must circulate and not concentrate in the hands of the few.

topics.name: The Quran as Source
topics.description: The primacy of the Quran as the first and foundational source of Islamic legislation.

topics.name: The Sunnah as Source
topics.description: The prophetic traditions (Sunnah/Hadith) as the second source of Islamic law.

topics.name: Permissible
topics.description: Halal and Mubah, acts and things explicitly permitted or left unrestricted in Islamic law.

topics.name: Prohibited
topics.description: Haram, acts and things explicitly forbidden in Islamic law, carrying sin and legal consequences.

topics.name: Dietary Laws
topics.description: Islamic regulations specifying permissible and forbidden foods and methods of slaughter.

topics.name: Intoxicants
topics.description: The absolute Islamic prohibition on alcohol, drugs, and all mind-altering substances.

topics.name: Gambling
topics.description: The Islamic prohibition on games of chance, betting, and all forms of speculative wagering.

topics.name: Hudud
topics.description: Fixed divinely prescribed punishments for specific major offenses mentioned in the Quran.

topics.name: Retribution
topics.description: Qisas, the principle of equal retaliation in cases of murder or physical injury.

topics.name: Blood Money
topics.description: Diyah, financial compensation paid to the victim's family as an alternative to or alongside Qisas.

topics.name: Witnesses and Evidence
topics.description: Islamic rules governing testimony, burden of proof, and the admissibility of evidence in legal proceedings.

topics.name: Jihad
topics.description: Striving in Allah's cause, encompassing both inner spiritual struggle and outward collective effort.

topics.name: Self-Defense
topics.description: The lawful right to defend oneself, family, and community against aggression.

topics.name: Rules of War
topics.description: The ethical and legal constraints governing conduct during armed conflict in Islam.

topics.name: Peace Treaties
topics.description: The legitimacy and conditions of entering into truces and peace agreements with adversaries.

topics.name: Migration for Faith
topics.description: Hijrah, the migration from a place of religious oppression to preserve one's faith and practice.

topics.name: Martyrdom
topics.description: The status of those killed in Allah's cause, their souls alive with their Lord, not to be called dead, a distinct theological category addressed directly in the Quran.

primary: killed in the way of Allah
do not say they are dead
those who die in Allah's cause
secondary: rejoicing in what Allah has given them
reward for those slain in His cause

topics.name: Leadership
topics.description: The Islamic conception of legitimate political and religious leadership through Khilafah or Imamah.

topics.name: Obedience to Authority
topics.description: The conditional Islamic obligation to obey legitimate rulers and those in authority.

topics.name: Accountability of Rulers
topics.description: The Islamic principle that leaders are accountable to Allah and to the community for just governance.

topics.name: Purification of the Heart
topics.description: Tazkiyat al-Nafs, the ongoing process of cleansing the soul from spiritual diseases and moral failings.

topics.name: Diseases of the Heart
topics.description: Amrad al-Qulub, spiritual pathologies such as envy, riya, and hardness of heart that corrupt the soul.

topics.name: Softness of Heart
topics.description: Leen al-Qalb, the tender, receptive heart moved by remembrance of Allah and Quranic recitation.

topics.name: Consciousness of Allah
topics.description: Taqwa, the ever-present awareness of Allah that motivates righteous action and restraint from sin.

topics.name: Contentment
topics.description: Qana'ah, inner satisfaction with what Allah has provided, free from restless craving.

topics.name: Repentance
topics.description: Tawbah, sincere turning away from sin toward Allah, meeting the conditions of genuine repentance.

topics.name: Return to Allah
topics.description: Inabah, a deeper, proactive turning of the entire self toward Allah in devotion.

topics.name: Hope in Allah's Mercy
topics.description: Raja, the spiritual state of confident hope in Allah's forgiveness and generosity.

topics.name: Fear of Allah
topics.description: Khawf and Khashyah, reverent awe and fear of Allah's punishment and displeasure.

topics.name: Balance of Hope and Fear
topics.description: The spiritually healthy state between Raja (hope) and Khawf (fear), avoiding both despair and false security.

topics.name: Struggling Against the Nafs
topics.description: Mujahadah, the deliberate effort to resist the soul's inclinations toward sin and heedlessness.

topics.name: Temptation
topics.description: The lures of worldly allure and shaytan's whispers that lead believers away from obedience.

topics.name: Worldly Attachment
topics.description: Hubb al-Dunya, excessive love of the material world that distracts from the Hereafter.

topics.name: Zuhd
topics.description: Ascetic detachment from the world, not owning less, but the world owning less of the heart.

topics.name: Yearning for Allah
topics.description: Shawq, an intense spiritual longing for closeness to Allah and for meeting Him in the Hereafter.

topics.name: Obedience to Allah
topics.description: Ta'ah, comprehensive submission to Allah's commands and prohibitions as the path to His nearness.

topics.name: Night Worship
topics.description: Qiyam al-Layl/Tahajjud, voluntary night prayers as a means of special closeness to Allah.

topics.name: Contemplation
topics.description: Tafakkur, the inner devotional act of sustained deep reflection as a form of worship that draws the believer into greater spiritual closeness with Allah.

topics.name: Spiritual Elevation
topics.description: The attainment of high spiritual stations (Maqamat) and nearness to Allah through sustained devotion.

topics.name: Death
topics.description: Mawt, the inevitable end of worldly life and separation of soul from body, the beginning of Akhirah.

topics.name: Life of the Grave
topics.description: Barzakh, the intermediate realm between death and resurrection, where souls experience bliss or punishment.

topics.name: Angel of Death
topics.description: Malak al-Mawt, the angel tasked with extracting souls at their appointed time of death.

topics.name: Resurrection
topics.description: Ba'ath, the raising of all humans from the dead for the final judgment.

topics.name: Reckoning
topics.description: Hisab, the precise divine accounting of every individual's deeds, words, and intentions.

topics.name: The Scale
topics.description: Mizan, the cosmic scales on which deeds are weighed to determine reward and punishment.

topics.name: Intercession
topics.description: Shafa'ah, the granted permission of the Prophet and others to intercede on behalf of believers on Judgment Day.

topics.name: Record of Deeds
topics.description: The written book of every person's deeds received in the right or left hand on Judgment Day.

topics.name: Abandonment by Family
topics.description: The Quranic depiction of family bonds dissolving on Judgment Day, each soul preoccupied with its own fate.

topics.name: Desperation and Pleading
topics.description: The desperate state of the disbeliever wishing to ransom themselves at any price to escape punishment.

topics.name: Minor Signs
topics.description: Early and ongoing prophesied signs indicating the approach of the Day of Judgment.

topics.name: Major Signs
topics.description: The ten or more dramatic cosmic events that immediately precede the establishment of the Hour.

topics.name: The Hour
topics.description: As-Sa'ah, the Day of Resurrection itself; the final and sudden termination of this world.

topics.name: Blowing of the Trumpet
topics.description: The two blasts of Israfil's trumpet, the first ending creation, the second resurrecting it.

topics.name: Description of Paradise
topics.description: Quranic and hadith depictions of Jannah, its gardens, rivers, palaces, and eternal life.

topics.name: Rewards of Paradise
topics.description: The specific physical and spiritual rewards promised to the inhabitants of Jannah.

topics.name: Seeing Allah
topics.description: Ru'yat Allah, the supreme reward of beholding Allah's face in Paradise, surpassing all other pleasures.

topics.name: Levels of Paradise
topics.description: The graduated ranks within Jannah, with Firdaws al-A'la as the highest station.

topics.name: Description of Hellfire
topics.description: Quranic depictions of Jahannam, its fire, depths, gates, and terrifying attributes.

topics.name: Punishments of Hell
topics.description: The specific torments described in the Quran and hadith for the inhabitants of Hellfire.

topics.name: People of the Fire
topics.description: The categories of individuals destined for Jahannam as described in revelation.

topics.name: Escape from Hellfire
topics.description: The means of salvation and deliverance from Hellfire through faith, deeds, and divine mercy.

topics.name: Divine Reward
topics.description: Thawab and Ajr, Allah's generous recompense for righteous acts, often multiplied manifold.

topics.name: Divine Punishment
topics.description: Adhab, Allah's precise retribution for sins and transgression, both in this world and the next.

topics.name: Regret on Judgment Day
topics.description: Hasrah, the overwhelming remorse of those who squandered their opportunities for righteousness.

topics.name: Divine Origin of the Quran
topics.description: The Quran as the literal, uncreated word (Kalam) of Allah revealed through Jibreel to the Prophet.

topics.name: Inimitability of the Quran
topics.description: I'jaz al-Quran, the Quran's miraculous linguistic, structural, and content-based inimitability, which no human can replicate.

topics.name: Preservation of the Quran
topics.description: Allah's guarantee that the Quran will remain unchanged and protected from alteration.

topics.name: Guidance of the Quran
topics.description: The Quran as the primary and complete guide for human life in all its dimensions.

topics.name: Healing through the Quran
topics.description: The Quran's curative function for spiritual diseases of the heart and its use in ruqyah.

topics.name: Wahy
topics.description: The process of divine inspiration and revelation, its modes, forms, and recipients.

topics.name: Stages of Revelation
topics.description: The gradual (Tadriji) nature of Quranic revelation over twenty-three years.

topics.name: Abrogation
topics.description: Naskh, the superseding of earlier Quranic rulings by later ones as part of Islamic legislative progression.

topics.name: Recitation of the Quran
topics.description: Tilawah and Tarteel, the proper, melodious, and measured oral rendering of the Quranic text.

topics.name: Pondering the Quran
topics.description: Tadabbur al-Quran, deep reflective engagement specifically with Quranic text to extract meaning, guidance, and wisdom from the revealed word.

topics.name: Following the Quran
topics.description: Ittiba, practically living by and implementing the Quranic teachings in daily life.

topics.name: Torah
topics.description: Tawrat, the scripture revealed to Musa, affirmed in the Quran and held to have been subsequently distorted.

topics.name: Gospel
topics.description: Injeel, the original scripture revealed to Isa, affirmed in the Quran as divine but subsequently altered.

topics.name: Psalms
topics.description: Zabur, the scripture revealed to Dawud, referenced in the Quran as a divine book.

topics.name: Distortion of Scriptures
topics.description: Tahrif, the Islamic doctrine that previous scriptures were textually or interpretively altered after revelation.

topics.name: Role of Prophets
topics.description: The divine mandate of prophets to convey Allah's message, establish proof, and guide humanity.

topics.name: Miracles of Prophets
topics.description: Mu'jizat, supernatural signs granted by Allah to prophets as evidential proof of their truthfulness.

topics.name: Seal of the Prophets
topics.description: Khatam al-Nabiyyin, the doctrine that Muhammad is the last and final prophet, closing prophethood.

topics.name: Following the Prophet
topics.description: Ittiba al-Rasul, the obligation to follow the Sunnah of the Prophet as a religious imperative.

topics.name: Rejection of Prophets
topics.description: The recurring Quranic theme of nations rejecting and opposing their prophets.

topics.name: Warning and Glad Tidings
topics.description: The dual prophetic function of delivering warnings of punishment and glad tidings of reward.

topics.name: Adam
topics.description: The story of Adam, creation, the covenant, the test in Paradise, and his status as first prophet.

topics.name: Nuh
topics.description: The story of Nuh (Noah), his long call to his people, the flood, and salvation on the Ark.

topics.name: Ibrahim
topics.description: The story of Ibrahim (Abraham), Khalilullah, the test of sacrifice, and the building of the Ka'bah.

topics.name: Musa
topics.description: The story of Musa (Moses), the confrontation with Pharaoh, Exodus, and receiving the Torah.

topics.name: Isa
topics.description: The story of Isa (Jesus), miraculous birth, prophethood, miracles, and elevation by Allah.

topics.name: Yusuf
topics.description: The story of Yusuf (Joseph), patience in adversity, betrayal, and rise to authority in Egypt.

topics.name: Dawud and Sulayman
topics.description: The stories of Dawud (David) and Sulayman (Solomon), prophets and kings granted unique gifts.

topics.name: Lut
topics.description: The Quranic narrative of Prophet Lut - his preaching against immorality, hosting of the angelic messengers, and the divine destruction of the people of Sodom. Appears across Surahs 11, 15, 26, 27.

topics.name: Al-Khidr
topics.description: The Quranic narrative of Musa's journey with the divinely-guided servant Al-Khidr (Surah 18:60-82), illustrating hidden divine wisdom operating beyond surface appearances.

topics.name: Dhul-Qarnayn
topics.description: The Quranic account of the righteous ruler Dhul-Qarnayn who traveled the earth, governed with justice, and built the iron barrier against Gog and Magog (Surah 18:83-98).

topics.name: Zakariyya and Yahya
topics.description: The Quranic narrative of Prophet Zakariyya's supplication for an heir, the miraculous birth of Yahya (John the Baptist), and both prophets' devotion (Surah 19:2-15).

topics.name: Other Prophets
topics.description: Quranic stories and mentions of other prophets including Salih, Hud, Shu'ayb, Yunus, Idris, Ayub, and others, each with unique narratives conveying moral and theological lessons.

topics.name: Hijrah to Madinah
topics.description: The pivotal migration of the Prophet and companions from Makkah to Madinah, marking a new era.

topics.name: Battles of the Prophet
topics.description: The military campaigns of the Prophet's era, Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, and others.

topics.name: Conquest of Makkah
topics.description: Fath Makkah, the peaceful liberation of Makkah in the 8th year of Hijrah.

topics.name: Ahl al-Bayt
topics.description: The household of the Prophet, referenced in the verse of purification (33:33) and the verse commanding love of the Prophet's close kin (42:23).

primary: Allah wishing to remove impurity from the Prophet's family
love of the Prophet's close kin
secondary: special status of the Prophet's family
reward of prophethood is love of kin

topics.name: The Companions (Sahabah)
topics.description: The Emigrants and Helpers, praised in the Quran as forerunners in faith, those who gave allegiance under the tree, and models of sacrifice and brotherhood.

primary: those who emigrated and those who gave them refuge
secondary: Allah being pleased with the companions
those who gave refuge to the migrants

topics.name: Prophetic Character
topics.description: Khuluq Adheem, the Prophet's supreme moral character, described as a living embodiment of the Quran.

topics.name: Prophetic Mercy
topics.description: Rahmatan lil Aalamin, the Prophet's mercy extending to all creation as his defining characteristic.

topics.name: Prophetic Wisdom
topics.description: The Prophet's unparalleled insight, strategic intelligence, and wise guidance in all matters.

topics.name: Love of the Prophet
topics.description: The obligatory love and veneration of the Prophet as a pillar of complete faith.

topics.name: Destroyed Nations
topics.description: Nations such as 'Ad, Thamud, and the people of Lut who were annihilated for rejecting their prophets.

topics.name: Pharaoh and His People
topics.description: Fir'awn and his court as the archetypal tyrant, whose arrogance led to destruction.

topics.name: People of the Book
topics.description: Ahl al-Kitab, Jews and Christians referenced in the Quran as previous recipients of revelation.

topics.name: Lessons from History
topics.description: Ibar, the moral and theological lessons drawn from Quranic accounts of past nations.

topics.name: Comforting the Prophet
topics.description: Verses in which Allah directly reassures and consoles the Prophet during hardship and rejection.

primary: your Lord has not forsaken you

topics.name: Relief of the Prophet's Burden
topics.description: Allah's removal of the weighty burden from the Prophet, a reference to Surah al-Inshirah.

topics.name: Elevation of the Prophet's Mention
topics.description: Allah's elevation of the Prophet's name and mention, referenced in Surah al-Inshirah.

topics.name: Instruction to the Prophet
topics.description: Direct Quranic commands to the Prophet concerning worship, proclamation, and conduct.

topics.name: Devotional Command to the Prophet
topics.description: Direct Quranic imperatives urging the Prophet toward intensified personal worship and devotion.

topics.name: Obligation of Seeking Knowledge
topics.description: The Islamic ruling that seeking fundamental religious knowledge is an individual obligation (Fard Ayn).

topics.name: Beneficial Knowledge
topics.description: Ilm Nafi, knowledge that benefits one in this life and the next, as opposed to harmful or useless learning.

topics.name: Knowledge and Action
topics.description: The Islamic principle that knowledge must be accompanied by corresponding practice.

topics.name: Scholars and Teachers
topics.description: The elevated status of Islamic scholars and teachers as inheritors of the prophets.

topics.name: Ignorance
topics.description: Jahl, the dangerous state of lacking religious knowledge, leading to misguidance and sin.

topics.name: Wisdom
topics.description: Hikmah, the capacity to discern truth, make sound judgments, and act in accordance with divine purpose.

topics.name: Intellect
topics.description: Aql, the human faculty of reason, which Islam affirms as a tool for understanding revelation and creation.

topics.name: Reflection on Creation
topics.description: Tafakkur fi al-Khalq, examining the natural world and cosmic phenomena as observable evidence pointing to Allah's existence, power, and wisdom.

topics.name: Heedlessness
topics.description: Ghaflah, the dangerous state of inattention and forgetfulness of Allah that leads to spiritual decline.

topics.name: Guidance from Allah
topics.description: Hidayah, the divine direction that leads the heart to truth, dependent on Allah's grace and human receptivity.

topics.name: Misguidance
topics.description: Dalal, straying from the straight path as a consequence of rejecting truth, following desires, or divine abandonment.

topics.name: The Straight Path
topics.description: Sirat al-Mustaqim, the correct, divinely ordained path of Islam that leads to Allah's pleasure and Paradise.

topics.name: Light and Darkness
topics.description: The Quranic metaphor of light representing guidance and darkness representing disbelief and misguidance.

topics.name: Sealing of Hearts
topics.description: Khatm ala al-Qulub, the divine sealing of hearts that persistently reject guidance.

topics.name: Calling with Wisdom
topics.description: Da'wah bil Hikmah, delivering the Islamic message with intelligence, tact, and situational sensitivity.

topics.name: Preaching and Admonition
topics.description: Maw'idhah Hasanah, offering reminders, exhortations, and good counsel to move hearts.

topics.name: Dialogue and Debate
topics.description: Mujadalah, engaging in respectful intellectual discourse to establish truth and address doubts.

topics.name: Patience in Da'wah
topics.description: The prophetically modelled virtue of persevering in dawah despite rejection, mockery, and opposition.

topics.name: Blind Following
topics.description: Taqlid, uncritical adherence to ancestral tradition without examining its validity against revelation.

secondary: what we found our fathers doing

topics.name: Denial of Truth
topics.description: Juhud, stubborn, willful rejection of the truth despite its clarity, driven by pride or interest.

topics.name: Mockery of Religion
topics.description: Istihza, ridiculing and making light of Islam, its adherents, or its revelations.

topics.name: Worldly Distraction
topics.description: Lahw, the diversion of attention from truth and faith by amusement, play, and worldly preoccupation.

topics.name: Satanic Deception
topics.description: The plots, whispers, and strategies of Iblis to misguide humanity and obstruct faith.

topics.name: Truth
topics.description: Haqq, absolute divine truth as embodied in revelation, the prophetic message, and the nature of reality.

topics.name: Falsehood
topics.description: Batil, all that is false, vain, or contrary to divine truth, destined to perish.

topics.name: Truth Prevails
topics.description: The Quranic assurance that Haqq will ultimately overcome and extinguish Batil.

topics.name: Creation of the Heavens and Earth
topics.description: The Quranic account of Allah creating the heavens and earth in six days as the foundation of existence.

topics.name: Creation of Humans
topics.description: The Quranic account of human creation, from clay, then a clot, and the breathing of the spirit into Adam.

topics.name: Creation of Jinn
topics.description: The Quranic account of jinn being created from smokeless fire, a separate created kind.

topics.name: Purpose of Creation
topics.description: The Quranic declaration that humans and jinn were created solely to worship Allah.

topics.name: Celestial Signs
topics.description: The sun, moon, stars, and cosmic order as divine signs for those who reflect.

topics.name: Water and Rain
topics.description: Allah's provision of rain, rivers, and seas as signs of His sustaining mercy.

topics.name: Earth and Mountains
topics.description: The earth's stability and mountains as signs of divine engineering for human habitation.

topics.name: Animals and Plants
topics.description: The diversity of animal life and vegetation as signs of Allah's creative power and provision.

topics.name: Day and Night
topics.description: The alternation of day and night as a cosmic sign of divine ordering and human benefit.

secondary: night for rest day for work

topics.name: Human Embryology as Divine Sign
topics.description: The Quran's description of human development in the womb, from a drop to a clinging clot to a lump of flesh, presented as a sign of Allah's creative power (23:12-14, 22:5).

primary: stages of human development in the womb
lump of flesh formed into bones
secondary: clinging clot to lump of flesh
created from a fluid then formed
human biology as evidence of divine power

topics.name: Ships and the Sea as Divine Sign
topics.description: The Quran's repeated use of ships sailing the sea and winds filling sails as signs of Allah's sustaining power and provision for humanity.

primary: sea made subservient to carry ships
winds driving ships as divine blessing
secondary: subjecting the ocean for human benefit

topics.name: Vicegerency on Earth
topics.description: Khalifah, the human being's role as Allah's steward and trustee on earth.

topics.name: Human Weakness
topics.description: The Quranic acknowledgment of human frailty, prone to error, forgetfulness, and haste.

topics.name: Human Dignity
topics.description: Karamah, the inherent honor and dignity bestowed upon human beings by Allah's creative act.

topics.name: Stages of Human Life
topics.description: The Quranic mention of the passage through childhood, youth, maturity, and old age.

topics.name: Soul and Spirit
topics.description: Ruh and Nafs, the spiritual dimensions of the human being as referenced in revelation.

secondary: knowledge of ruh is with Allah

topics.name: Divine Blessings
topics.description: Ni'mah, the countless specific and general favors Allah has bestowed upon humanity.

topics.name: Provision from Allah
topics.description: Rizq, all forms of sustenance, livelihood, and provision decreed and delivered by Allah.

topics.name: Testing through Blessings
topics.description: The Quranic principle that abundance, wealth, and health are themselves tests of gratitude and proper use.

topics.name: Trials through Hardship
topics.description: Divine tests that come in the form of loss, suffering, poverty, illness, or calamity.

topics.name: Trials through Prosperity
topics.description: The less recognized but equally serious test of wealth, health, and ease.

topics.name: Trials of Faith
topics.description: Tests directed specifically at one's belief, persecution, pressure to abandon faith, religious adversity.

topics.name: Trials of the Prophets
topics.description: The Quranic emphasis on prophets enduring the most severe trials as models for believers.

topics.name: Patience in Hardship
topics.description: Sabr, the prescribed response to external trials, loss, and affliction: enduring without complaint to other than Allah.

secondary: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi rajiun

topics.name: Seeking Help through Prayer
topics.description: The Quranic directive to seek strength through patience and prayer when facing difficulty.

topics.name: Despair
topics.description: Ya's and Qunut, the prohibited state of losing all hope in Allah's mercy, condemned in the Quran.

secondary: do not despair of Allah's mercy

topics.name: Purification through Trials
topics.description: Tamhis, trials as a means of expiation for sins and purification of the soul.

topics.name: Distinguishing Believers
topics.description: Tamyiz, trials serve to distinguish true, sincere faith from mere outward profession.

secondary: who truly believes revealed in trial

topics.name: Return to Allah through Trials
topics.description: The way hardship wakes the heedless and returns the straying believer to Allah.

topics.name: Parables and Similitudes (Mathal)
topics.description: The Quran's use of explicit parables and analogies to illustrate theological and moral truths, verses containing 'their likeness is as...' or 'the example of...'

primary: parable of good word and bad word
secondary: example of one who kindles fire

topics.name: Rhetorical Questions
topics.description: Verses in which Allah poses questions not seeking an answer but to provoke reflection, establish proof, or challenge denial.

secondary: which of the favors of your Lord will you deny
then what message after this will they believe

topics.name: Muqattaat
topics.description: The isolated, abbreviated letters at the beginning of certain Surahs, whose meaning is known only to Allah.

topics.name: Quranic Oath
topics.description: The divine oaths in the Quran sworn by created phenomena to emphasize profound truths.

topics.name: Maryam (Mary)
topics.description: The only woman named in the Quran, mother of Isa, model of purity and devotion, subject of an entire surah and multiple passages.

topics.name: Wife of Pharaoh (Asiyah)
topics.description: The wife of Pharaoh who believed in Musa, interceded to spare the infant Musa's life, and is cited as a model for all believers with her prayer for a house in Paradise.

topics.name: Queen of Sheba (Bilqis)
topics.description: The unnamed queen in Surah al-Naml whose encounter with Solomon and ultimate submission to Allah is a narrative of sovereignty, wisdom, and guidance.

primary: throne of Sheba brought to Solomon

topics.name: Wife of Imran (Mother of Maryam)
topics.description: The woman who dedicated her unborn child to Allah's service, her vow, its acceptance, and the birth of Maryam as an answered prayer.

primary: wife of Imran dedicating child to God

topics.name: Wives of the Prophet
topics.description: The Mothers of the Believers, addressed directly in the Quran with specific rulings, obligations, and elevated spiritual status.

secondary: modest conduct required of Prophet's wives

topics.name: Spiritual Equality of Men and Women
topics.description: The Quranic declaration that men and women are equal before Allah in faith, deeds, and reward, no gender distinction in divine accountability.

primary: men and women equal before Allah
equal reward for believing men and women
secondary: no spiritual superiority based on gender
whoever does good male or female
righteous deeds rewarded regardless of gender
spiritual rank not determined by gender

topics.name: Modesty and Hijab
topics.description: The Quranic injunctions on modesty of dress and gaze for both men and women, including lowering the gaze and covering adornments.

topics.name: Women's Financial and Marital Rights
topics.description: Quranic provisions protecting women, the obligatory dower, the right to initiate divorce, and prohibition of inheriting women against their will.

topics.name: Common Ground with People of the Book
topics.description: The Quranic call to a word of common ground between Muslims and People of the Book, shared monotheism as a basis for dialogue.

primary: come to a word common between us
common ground with Christians and Jews
inviting People of the Book to worship Allah alone
secondary: do not take lords besides Allah
shared belief with People of the Book

topics.name: Critique of Distorted Beliefs
topics.description: The Quran's theological critique of specific doctrinal errors among People of the Book, the Trinity, claiming Jesus or Ezra as son of God.

primary: correcting theological errors of People of the Book
secondary: associating partners with Allah by Christians and Jews

topics.name: No Compulsion in Religion
topics.description: The Quranic principle that faith cannot be forced, each person is accountable for their own religious choice.

primary: to you your religion to me mine
secondary: right guidance is distinct from error
your deeds are yours mine are mine

topics.name: Justice toward Non-Muslims
topics.description: The Quranic command to deal equitably and kindly with non-Muslims who are not at war with believers.

primary: do not wrong those who did not fight you
secondary: fair treatment of those who seek peace

topics.name: Prohibition of Corruption on Earth
topics.description: The Quranic prohibition of spreading corruption and destruction on earth, used in verses condemning hypocrites, tyrants, and those who destroy crops and lives.

primary: those who make mischief on earth
secondary: do not corrupt after it was set right
corruption on earth as major sin
ruin and destruction on earth forbidden

topics.name: Animals as Communities
topics.description: The Quranic declaration that animals and birds are communities like humans, affirming their status as created beings with their own relationship to Allah.

primary: every beast and bird is a community
secondary: birds and beasts as created communities

topics.name: Prohibition of Waste and Excess
topics.description: The Quranic prohibition of wasting resources and squandering, applied to food, wealth, and the bounties of the earth.

primary: eat and drink but not to excess
secondary: Allah does not love those who waste

topics.name: Israa and Mi'raj
topics.description: The Prophet's miraculous night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem and his ascension through the heavens, referenced in Surah al-Israa (17:1) and Surah al-Najm (53:13-18).

primary: night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem
glorified is He who took His servant by night
Prophet seeing signs of Allah on ascension
secondary: lote tree of the utmost boundary

topics.name: Prophetic Dreams
topics.description: True prophetic dreams as a form of divine communication, Ibrahim's vision of sacrificing his son, Joseph's dreams, and the Prophet's vision of entering Makkah.

primary: Abraham's dream of sacrificing his son
secondary: dream of seven fat and lean cows
Prophet's true vision of entering Makkah

topics.name: Sanctity of the Sacred Mosque
topics.description: The Quranic sanctification of the Sacred Mosque and the Farthest Mosque, as the first houses of worship, direction of prayer, and sites of prophetic history.

secondary: wrongdoing forbidden in the sacred mosque
first house of worship on earth
Abraham raising foundations of the Kaaba
prayer direction toward the Sacred Mosque
